core_obligations: Identify the set of closed points: if the space is finite this set is finite, and by hypothesis it is finite in the second case as well (proof lines 3683-3685)
Its closure is everything: the Jacobson property makes the closed points dense (proof lines 3686-3687)

Closedness: a finite set is a finite union of singletons, which are closed, hence the set of closed points is closed and therefore all of the space, so every point is closed and, by finiteness, also open (proof lines 3687-3690)
proof_roadmap: 设 X_0 为闭点集；有限空间时 X_0 有限，第二种情形按假设也有限。
由 Jacobson 性质，闭包(X_0) = X。
X_0 是有限个单点闭集之并 ⇒ 闭 ⇒ X = X_0 ⇒ 每点闭；又 X 有限 ⇒ 每点开 ⇒ 离散。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a finite Jacobson space, and more generally a Jacobson space with finitely many closed points, is discrete (author lemma at source lines 3677-3681, label lemma-finite-jacobson). The proof (source lines 3683-3691) shows that the set of closed points is dense by the Jacobson property and closed as a finite union of singletons, hence is the whole space, after which finiteness makes every point open (proof lines 3683-3690). The density-and-closedness argument is the content. H2.
